title: v1-chat: adaptive-response-chunking-role-preservation-and-functioncall-backpressure
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers using the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer have reported inconsistent role boundaries and fragmented tool/function-call payloads when we slice large responses into stream chunks. This causes downstream consumers (websocket clients, tool runners) to misinterpret partial function call JSON and to issue duplicate invocations. Additionally, we observed higher-than-expected token usage from clients that retry on partial logprob messages. This PR introduces an adaptive response chunking layer that preserves role/message integrity, reconciles stop token semantics across model variants, and adds a simple function-call handshake + backpressure headers for clients to avoid duplicate tool execution.

Summary of changes: adaptive chunking algorithm that expands chunk boundaries to nearest safe token/byte boundary while ensuring role/message atomicity; stop-token reconciliation that prefers earliest explicit stop but falls back to model-end heuristics when needed; logprob envelope migration to avoid emitting partial logprob arrays mid-token; lightweight fncall handshake over stream where the runtime includes a fncall-intent envelope and the client must ACK before executor runs; add Retry-After and X-Stream-Window headers to help clients back off when underlying GPU queue is saturated.

Design notes: the adaptive chunker uses a model-agnostic tokenizer window to find safe cut points; when a cut would split a role-delimited message, the chunker expands until the full message is included or maximum window (8KB) is hit. For function calls we emit a 3-stage envelope: INTENT -> ACK_REQUIRED flag -> FINAL payload. The default is ACK_REQUIRED=true for dedicated and private deployments; hosted deployments set a config flag for opt-in to reduce latency tradeoffs. Stop token logic is layered: explicit stop overrides everything; for incompatible model variants we map stop arrays to the most permissive interpretation and include a stop-mapping header in the stream metadata to aid debugging.

Checklist: [x] adaptive chunker algorithm and unit tests, [x] stream format upgrade and backwards-compatible decoder, [x] fncall-intent handshake and ack path, [x] headers for backpressure, [x] e2e test harness with simulated slow consumer, [x] docs update draft for API changes.

Testing and rollout: included unit + integration tests cover 95% of chunking edge cases and a small scale canary in staging with 2% traffic routed to the new stream coordinator. We ran synthetic workloads with a slow websocket consumer and confirmed no duplicate function invocations across 10k simulated conversations. Rollout plan: enable opt-in for hosted via feature flag for 1 week, then enable by default for dedicated/private after customer notifications. Rollback: config toggle disables ACK_REQUIRED and reverts to legacy chunker.

Related: Linear ENG-67890 (streaming/tool-safety), ENG-70112 (openaicompat stop-mapping).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can the chunker make deterministic choices across model versions? Suggest we persist a small chunking seed in model metadata so edge-case diffs are reproducible.
Author (Sofia Patel): Added model metadata seed; deterministic mode gated behind DEBUG_CHUNKER env var to avoid perf regression in hot paths.
Mei Chen: ACK_REQUIRED defaulting to true worries me for hosted latency-sensitive customers. Recommend feature-flag and opt-in in hosted while enabled by default in Dedicated/Private.
Author: Implemented wired feature flag and updated console flag UI; documented latency tradeoff in compatibility doc.
Diego Rivera: Tests look good; one flaky e2e on CI related to simulated network jitter — added additional retries and trimmed the harness timing to be less brittle.
Security (automated): serialization of fncall payload sanitized; safe-guarded against header injection.
release_notes: Improved OpenAI /v1/chat streaming parity: adaptive chunking to preserve role/message boundaries, reliable function-call handshake to avoid duplicate executions, better stop-token reconciliation across model variants, and stream-level backpressure headers for client coordination. Backwards compatible; opt-in for hosted via feature flag.
notes_for_ops: Enable stream_adaptive_chunking feature flag in staging before rolling to prod.
Add alert: stream.chunker.expand_rate > 0.05 for 5m indicating frequent boundary expansions.
Ensure console flag rollout has customer notification for Dedicated/Private customers.
deployment_summary: Canary: 2% traffic to new stream coordinator for 72 hours
Stage: 10% for 48 hours with synthetic slow-consumer test enabled
Prod: gradual ramp to 100% after checks pass; hosted default opt-in for first week
